definitions: A yellowish or brownish bitter-tasting organic substance present in some galls, barks, and other plant tissues, used in leather production and ink manufacture.

Any of a group of astringent, bitter plant polyphenols that bind to and precipitate proteins and other organic compounds including amino acids and alkaloids. The term tannin is widely used to refer to any large polyphenolic compound containing sufficient hydroxyls and other suitable groups (e.g., carboxyls) to form strong complexes with protein and other macromolecules.
examples: Tannins are responsible for the astringency in tea.
Oak barrels impart tannins to the whiskey.
